findings.summary: Recurrence is judged by the introspection's recorded time, not by whether the failing job ran on a tree that already had the fix.
findings.evidence: A job could be built on a base from before the landing but introspected after it. That job would count as a recurrence and cause a re-queue the fix may already cover. A more exact rule would compare the introspected job's base commit with the landing's through_commit or candidate_commit. The accepted reading chose the timestamp rule on purpose, to mirror the closed-by-person branch, and the cost is an extra queued request, not lost work. So this is minor, not major.

findings.summary: `later.at = at(600)` in the new test does nothing.
findings.evidence: The introspection(n, ..) helper already sets `at: at(n)` (line 3925).

summary: The change does what the accepted reading asked: it fixes review finding 2. A landed request now stops addressing a failure cause once an introspection of that cause is recorded after the landing, using the same comparison the closed-by-person branch already makes. An open request still addresses the cause. I ran `cargo test -p athena-core hestia`: all 87 tests passed, including the two new ones, which cover a recurrence after the landing, a landing after the newest introspection, and an open request with newer introspections. I also ran `cargo test -p athena-core`: 1419 passed and 1 was ignored. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and test checks passed in CI for this commit. The module doc, the function doc and CHANGELOG.md all describe the new rule, and only the two expected files changed. One existing backfill fixture now lands its request at 2000 s, which the new rule requires; the test still checks the landed request it was written for. One minor finding: recurrence is judged by when an introspection was recorded, so a job that started before the fix landed but failed after it can trigger an extra re-queue. Comparing the job's base commit with the landing would be more exact, but the accepted reading chose the timestamp rule on purpose. Two nits are cosmetic. Verdict: pass.
